summary: On August 12, 2026 the IRS released Notice 2026-49, proposing sample forms and standardized procedures for rollovers between employer retirement plans and IRAs under SECURE 2.0 Section 324 (IRA-to-IRA transfers aren't covered). It's still a draft: the IRS is taking public comments through October 23, 2026, so nothing is final or mandatory yet.
suggestedAction: No action needed now. When you eventually roll your 401(k)/403(b) over to an IRA at retirement, expect a more standardized paperwork process; revisit once the IRS finalizes the procedure.

source: Analysis of employer pay stub + Truthifi transaction history
summary: Updated 2026-09-13 with prior-year evidence: employee 401(k) elective deferrals are on pace to reach the 2026 IRS limit within the next 1-2 pay periods, driven partly by a variable quarterly bonus that also has 401(k) withheld. A same pay-stub review of the equivalent December 2025 period shows the same pattern already played out once: employee deferrals stopped after hitting the 2025 limit exactly, and the employer Safe Harbor contribution stopped in that same pay period rather than continuing independently — the signature of no per-period true-up. That single pay stub can't rule out a later lump-sum true-up correction (some plans issue one in the year's final payroll or the following January).
suggestedAction: Check the prior year's final pay stub (or W-2 Box 12 Code D/AA total) against that year's IRS limit exactly: a total matching the limit exactly means no true-up occurred; a total exceeding it means a true-up correction was made afterward. Also confirm directly with HR/the Summary Plan Description whether a true-up provision exists going forward. If none exists, consider reducing next year's per-paycheck percentage so contributions spread evenly across all pay periods instead of maxing out early.
